The 2026 FIFA World Cup was jointly hosted by Canada, Mexico, and the United States across 16 cities.
Spain won the championship for the second time by defeating Argentina 1–0 in extra time during the final.
Kylian Mbappé of France won the Golden Boot with 10 goals, becoming the all-time leading goalscorer at the World Cup.
Rodri of Spain was awarded the Golden Ball as the best player, while Unai Simón won the Golden Glove.
Pau Cubarsí of Spain received the FIFA Young Player Award as the tournament's best young player.
The tournament expanded to 48 teams from 32, featuring 104 matches played over 39 days.
The 2026 World Cup introduced new rules including 10-second substitutions and 5-second restarts for throw-ins and goal kicks.
Mandatory three-minute hydration breaks were introduced in every half for all matches during the tournament.
The draw for the 48 teams took place on December 5, 2025, at the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C.
The official match ball was named Adidas Trionda, featuring red, green, and blue colors representing the host nations.
The tournament mascots were Maple the Moose, Zayu the Jaguar, and Clutch the Bald Eagle.
Total attendance reached 6,810,966 spectators, setting a new record for the highest cumulative attendance in World Cup history.
The tournament generated a record $15 billion in revenue and distributed $871 million in prize money.
FIFA signed deals with TikTok and YouTube to serve as preferred platforms for streaming World Cup content.
The official song "Dai Dai" was performed by Shakira and Burna Boy, followed by the anthem "DNA (More Than a Game)".
